findings.reason: the section must either carry the `saw_live` hinge into the station/subscriber contract or add the arming-before-pointer case and its control to the done-when; without it a node implements §10 literally and reintroduces the dispatch-settles-its-own-follower race the current code exists to prevent.
findings.text: the drain-settle measure settles a subscriber on "the station's readings for all of its populations have read no live work for the grace" and declares three drain-settle controls (own-session-only, ownerless/unscoped, no-grace handover), but none of the four covers a subscriber armed while its populations are *already* empty: today `_check_settle` refuses to settle at all until it has seen live work (`saw_live` stays false and the function returns, reckon/crew_follow_commands.py:1495, 1555, with the reason stated in the code: "a dispatch asks the host for this follower before it publishes the run's pointer, so a follower that settled on its first empty reading would leave before its own run appeared"). A station that records a per-(project, session) "no live work" reading from its first tick will have carried that reading for longer than the grace by the time a freshly armed subscriber first polls, so the subscriber settles and exits before the dispatch that armed it publishes its run's pointer — and every case and negative control §10 declares still passes, because not one of them arms a subscriber against an empty population.

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — each symbol §10 cites resolves at this revision: `resumption.sweep` (reckon/crew/resumption.py:1768, no host filter, session-scoped only, as the section claims), `runs.sweep_unfollowed_sessions` (reckon/crew/runs.py:3746, whose docstring states the host rule §10 borrows), `recovery_review_acceptance.dispatch_awaiting_reviews` (recovery_review_acceptance.py:377), `recovery_review_dispatch.review_settle_seconds_remaining` (:1258, reading `auto_resume` alone as claimed), `recovery_review_dispatch._latest_resume_at` (:206, returning the newer of the two stamps), `_check_settle`/`_population_has_live_work`/`settle_populations`/`FOLLOWER_SETTLE_SAMPLE_SECONDS`/`FOLLOWER_SETTLE_GRACE_SECONDS` (reckon/crew_follow_commands.py:482, 1505, 1517, 285, 312). No `<a href>` in §10 to resolve.
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — the drain-settle measure (plan.html:319-322) carries no case for a subscriber armed while its populations already read no live work, so the mechanism it specifies can drop `_check_settle`'s `saw_live` hinge and still pass every case and negative control the section declares.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — §10 declares no implementation gate paths (it is the authored plan), and what it does point a later reader at are repository modules and symbols rather than a temporary or session-local location.
rubric_items.naming: pass — §10 names no plan label, stage name or ticket number in a symbol, and "old §81" is a carried-section reference in plan prose, which is the plan's own cross-reference grammar rather than code naming.
rubric_items.reasoning: pass — all three checks hold on the text as written: the stated cause (per-follower redundant sweep and settle reads) is the one the section's own cited callers show (`resumption.sweep` per follower, `_check_settle` scanning `_list_live_records` per second), the mechanisms produce the measured outcomes, and the production caller is named (the station's tick loop, §7). The one gap — the `saw_live` hinge the replacement mechanism would drop — is reported under `done_when`, because it is the measure's missing case that lets it through.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — "the review reflex and settle run once, in the station" is one move: both per-follower cadences become the station's, and the advice-door settle reader is the same mechanism reached from the other side.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — §10's `plan-section-depends-on` entry declares s7 and s8 (plan.html:23), both of which exist, and the two nodes it names are exactly the ones its measure needs: the station that runs the sweep (§7) and the subscriber whose trace it takes (`the process §8 delivers`, plan.html:328).
